name: manual_7d1a08
claim: When a test fails and you cannot explain it, debug the harness before the code: reproduce on pristine main under the same environment, change one factor at a time, read the child process stderr, sweep for the whole class once one instance is found, prove new tests with a mutant, and state your own harness errors out loud.

decisions.notes: Two of three apparent failures were first attributed to the change under test; both reproduced identically on pristine origin/main. One was briefly caused by my own PYTHONPATH override replacing the checkout path. Removing the load-bearing line (bind and drain) and watching the new tests fail is what showed they actually bite.
